hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches a tenant leak planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plant T2 adds a per-user-id cache, captured by a closure, to GET /api/identity/users/{id}/access, which is this piece's "what can this person do" endpoint. The whole gate suite still passes 62/62 (plants/plant-T2.log), and so do the identity, kernel and tenancy suites (plant-T2-other-suites.log). The proof test shows tenant A's admin getting 200 with tenant B admin's roles and permissions (plants/plant-T2-proof.log). The static-field variant T1 was caught only by the process-state inventory; the HTTP attack missed the leaked body (plants/plant-T1.log). Plant U, a global unique e-mail index, was caught, but only incidentally: G1SignInThrottle creates the same e-mail in two workspaces (plant-U-full-suite.log).

hard_gates.gate: G2 gate catches a permission fault planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plant P1 guards POST /users/{id}/unblock with identity.signIns.read, a read permission. Plant P2 drops the within-own-grants check on DELETE /roles/{id}. With both in place, G2 runs 15 of 16 passing (the one failure is P3's) and the identity tests pass 32/32 (plants/plant-P.log). The proof shows a user holding only signIns.read and users.read gets 204 from unblock, and a user holding only roles.delete and roles.read deletes a role granting users.create, users.update and resetPassword with 204 (plants/plant-P-proof.log). A UI plant that shows Delete role regardless of roles.delete passes 74/74 web unit tests, and no e2e spec opens Roles as such a user (plants/plant-UI.log).

biggest_gap.title: The G1 gate misses a cross-tenant leak through this piece's own "what can this person do" endpoint
biggest_gap.detail:
A per-user-id cache on GET /api/identity/users/{id}/access, held in a local that the endpoint lambda captures, hands tenant B's roles and permissions to tenant A's admin. All 62 gate tests still pass. Two blind spots combine.

(1) The process-state inventory skips compiler-generated types, so closure state is never listed. This was reported in p01 r2 and is still open at this commit.

(2) The HTTP attack cannot see a per-id cache even when the leak is in the response body. TenantActivity.OwnPathAsync warms each route with one tenant B id per collection. IsolationAttack then attacks with up to 5 snapshot ids per table plus the tenant id, so the ids A attacks are seldom the ids B just warmed. With the static variant (T1), the HTTP attack also passed; only the reflection inventory caught it.

Fix:
- Feed the exact route values tenant B used into tenant A's route attack, and have B touch every victim id before A attacks it.
- List fields of closure display classes reachable from endpoint delegates, or forbid captured mutable locals in endpoint mapping.
- Add self-tests for a closure cache and a per-id cache on a route with an id.
biggest_gap.evidence:
In a clone of 5a711de:

1. Apply gauntlet/evidence/p03-identity/r1/plants/plant-T2-closure-access-cache.diff.
2. Run `dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release`. It reports Passed 62 of 62 (plants/plant-T2.log). The identity, kernel and tenancy suites also pass (plant-T2-other-suites.log).
3. Copy plants/CriticPlantProof.cs into tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/CriticProof/ and run with --filter CriticPlantProof. Tenant B's admin reads its own access view, then tenant A's admin calls GET /api/identity/users/{B admin id}/access, gets 200, and receives B's Administrator role id and permission list (plants/plant-T2-proof.log).

The static variant plants/plant-T1-static-access-cache.diff passes G1HttpIsolation and fails only G1ProcessState (plants/plant-T1.log).

other_findings: [route: p00-foundation] G2 trusts each endpoint's declared permission. A write guarded by a read permission passes every gate: plant P1 puts identity.signIns.read on POST /users/{id}/unblock. The seeded Read-only role holds signIns.read, so any read-only user could clear sign-in pauses (plants/plant-P-proof.log). This is the same class as p01 r2's D2 and is still open at this commit.

[route: p00-foundation] The HTTP attack checks for differential answers on GETs only. A global unique e-mail index (plant U) makes POST /api/identity/users answer 409 for tenant B's address and 201 for an unused one, which tells tenant A which addresses B uses (plants/plant-U-proof.txt). It was caught only because G1SignInThrottle happens to create the same e-mail in two workspaces. The database gate also never looks at unique indexes on tenant tables that leave out tenant_id.
[route: p00-foundation] Response headers other than Location are still not judged, so the p01 r2 header-leak gap is not fixed at this commit (G1HttpIsolationTests.cs passes only Location to Judge).

This piece's own G2 gaps:
- The takeover and grant-escalation gates cover only /users/{id} and POST /roles/{id}/copy. DELETE /roles/{id} without its within-own-grants check (plant P2) passes, so a user with only roles.delete can delete roles granting permissions they lack.
- The screens-hide-what-you-cannot-do check has no case for the Roles screen. Showing Delete role regardless of roles.delete passes 74/74 web unit tests, and no e2e spec opens Roles as a user who lacks roles.delete.

Scope gap: there is no per-user default company and no per-company role assignment. No company concept exists at this commit, and identity.user_roles has no company column. The piece spec requires both. For UAE groups running several LLC or free-zone entities, a role that cannot be limited to one company is the main thing a restricted role needs.

find-user loses on a keystroke tie, 24 against 24. Search is one contiguous ILIKE string. Word-order-independent multi-word search ("rania kaabi" is 11 keys), or focusing the search box when Users opens, would beat Odoo outright.
create-restricted-user: no module permission beyond identity and workspace exists, so the task's "contacts only" role cannot be built yet. The win was measured with the Read-only role.

Users list:
- No sort, no filter by role, status or inactive, and no export.
- Offset paging only.
- Search is a full ILIKE scan taking 0.21 to 0.25 s at 100,004 rows, with no trigram index (users-search-timings.txt).
- The list is hand-built, not the shared list framework.

Users cannot be deleted, and the e-mail cannot be changed after creation. A typo in an invitation leaves an orphan account. Odoo lets the login be edited. The ours driver had to remove its test user through the database.

Arabic layout defects:
- The sign-in history table overflows the user panel, so the Session column is cut off, and the paused-until line has broken bidi order (screenshot 07).
- The inactive status cell is clipped at the list edge (screenshot 04).
- The matrix "Change" header is clipped in English (screenshot 03).
- Users have one display name with no Arabic name, so the Arabic list shows Latin names even though the shared dataset carries name_ar.

Lockout works per client. After 6 failures the right password is refused from that client, and the admin sees the pause with "allow sign-in again" (lockout-and-history.txt). Behind Docker every client arrives as 172.19.0.1, and compose sets no KnownProxies. A deployment that misses the README setting therefore lets one attacker pause an account for the whole office.

The seeded Read-only role includes identity.signIns.read, so every read-only user sees all colleagues' IP addresses and browsers. identity.sign_in_attempts has no retention. These are personal data under UAE PDPL; worth an owner decision.

identity.verify_sign_in takes the throttle source as a parameter from the app role. With any SQL injection, the per-client throttle could be bypassed by rotating p_source. An address that exists in two workspaces costs two PBKDF2 derivations, so timing shows it is used in more than one workspace.

Positive:
- Tenant isolation held in every API and database attack.
- Audit covers users, roles, user_roles, credentials (redacted) and sessions.
- Arabic is right to left from sign-in (dir=rtl, lang=ar), with no Latin words on the Arabic roles screen.
- No console errors or 5xx during the walk.
- Test counts rose from p00 r2's 126/19/9 to 158/74/24 plus 68 compare tests, and the ratchet holds.

Harness note: verify's Testcontainers bind random host ports outside the critic's assigned block, which cannot be overridden. Comparing find-user needs ERP_SEED_USERS_CSV. The added find-user task and drivers are in compare-drivers/ for the recorder to merge.
